Shir HaShirim and Metaphors for God
sheets.summary:
This sourcesheet is for an arts based Hillel lesson: 

1. Start out by asking what color(s) God might represents. Pass out watercolor or other art supplies. You can also talk about color theory, and the way colors hold different emotions or possibilities. 

2. Explain that ShS is traditionally read on Passover, and can be read both allegorically and literally. This shuir takes it in an allegorical direction. 

3. Work through the sources with students or give them hevruta time to explore them on their own. What do the sources say about relationships? About sexuality and desire? How can we read that into God? --- NOTE: ShS is hyper hetro-normative. make sure to address that. 

4. Go back to the art supplies. How has ShS changed or altered your image of God? What new emotions or colors do you want to bring in? Students can either make a second painting or work on top of their first painting. If there's time, give students a chance to share what they made and why.

en.title: The Delight of Love
en.prompt: The Song of Songs passionately expresses love, comparing it to the delight of wine. This poetic and allegorical book, attributed to Solomon, is traditionally understood as a metaphor for the loving relationship between God and the people of Israel.

description.en: [Song of Songs](https://www.sefaria.org/Song_of_Songs?tab=contents) (“Shir Hashirim”) is one of the five megillot (scrolls), part of the section of the Hebrew Bible called Writings. Attributed in its opening verse to [King Solomon](https://www.sefaria.org/topics/king-solomon?tab=sources), the book records poetic conversations between two lovers, describing their pursuit of each other through vineyards and fields of blossoming flowers. It is traditionally understood as a metaphor for the loving relationship between God and the people of Israel, and is often read publicly on Passover or on Shabbat evening.

[Song of Songs](https://www.sefaria.org/Song_of_Songs?tab=contents) (“Shir Hashirim”) is one of the five megillot (scrolls), part of the section of the Hebrew Bible called Writings. Attributed in its opening verse to [King Solomon](https://www.sefaria.org/topics/king-solomon?tab=sources), the book records poetic conversations between two lovers, describing their pursuit of each other through vineyards and fields of blossoming flowers. It is traditionally understood as a metaphor for the loving relationship between God and the people of Israel, and is often read publicly on Passover or on Shabbat evening.

Solomon was the third king of the United Kingdom of Israel and the son of [King David](https://www.sefaria.org/topics/king-david?tab=admin). Best known for building the first [Temple](https://www.sefaria.org/topics/beit-hamikdash?) in Jerusalem, he also built up the kingdom and expanded Israelite borders. Known for his wisdom, the authorship of the book of Proverbs, Song of Songs, and Ecclesiastes are traditionally attributed to him.

description.he: שלמה הוא המלך השני בשושלת דוד, והוא נודע בייחוד בזכות בניית בית המקדש בירושלים. כמו כן בנה ממלכה מפוארת והרחיב את גבולות ישראל. הוא ידוע בתור מלך חכם בצורה יוצאת דופן, וספרי התנ"ך משלי, שיר השירים וקהלת מיוחסים לו.

description.en: [Song of Songs](https://www.sefaria.org/Song_of_Songs?tab=contents) (“Shir Hashirim”) is one of the five megillot (scrolls), part of the section of the Hebrew Bible called Writings. Attributed in its opening verse to [King Solomon](https://www.sefaria.org/topics/king-solomon?tab=sources), the book records poetic conversations between two lovers, describing their pursuit of each other through vineyards and fields of blossoming flowers. It is traditionally understood as a metaphor for the loving relationship between God and the people of Israel, and is often read publicly on Passover or on Shabbat evening.

Many biblical characters are described as loving their spouses or children. The Torah commands people to love in specific contexts – like loving one’s fellow, the stranger, and God – and [Song of Songs](https://www.sefaria.org/Song_of_Songs?tab=contents) consists of poetic conversations between two lovers. Jewish texts composed over thousands of years explore the wonders, hardships, and practical manifestations of love.
description.he: דמויות מקראיות רבות מתוארות כאוהבות את בני זוגן או ילדיהן. התורה מצווה על אנשים לאהוב בהקשרים ספציפיים - כמו אהבת הזולת, הגר והאל וגם פרקי מגילת שיר השירים הם למעשה שיח של שירה בין שני אוהבים. מקורות יהדות שנכתבו לאורך הדורות עוסקים בביטויים המעשיים של אהבה וגם בקשיים שבה.
